title: spec: jmap-chat-mimi hard-requires a Basic credential, so did:webvh and RFC 9420 x509 cannot be used through it
description:
Found 2026-11-23 reading draft-atwood-jmap-chat-mimi-00. Two of Mark's
own drafts contradict each other. His call.

THE BINDING FORBIDS ANYTHING BUT BASIC. Not an omission -- an active
rejection:

- §keypackage line 314: the server "MUST reject the record with
  `invalidProperties` naming `keyPackage` ... if its credential is not a
  Basic credential ({{RFC9420, Section 5.3}})".
- §senders line 155: "The sender's MIMI user URI is the identity of the
  Basic credential ({{RFC9420, Section 5.3}}) in the MLS sender's leaf."
  No rule is given for a leaf carrying anything else.

And the document mentions did:webvh, x509 and X.509 exactly ZERO times
(checked case-insensitively).

WHAT THAT EXCLUDES:

1. draft-atwood-mls-didwebvh-credential, Mark's own draft, implemented in
   this repo as the mls-didwebvh crate. Its whole purpose is to give a
   user a credential stronger than Basic, since AGENTS.md records the
   deliberate weakness that "a provider can claim any identity for its
   own users unless they use the did:webvh credential
   (mimid-1wgh.4.81)". A client holding exactly that credential cannot
   publish a KeyPackage through this JMAP binding at all: the server is
   required to reject it.
2. RFC 9420 §5.3's `x509` credential, which is standards-track MLS and
   which mimid also does not implement (bead mimid-7yn7.4.1).

So the binding that mimid's agent uses to reach its provider forecloses
the identity work the rest of the project treats as the remedy for its
main known weakness.

NOTE WHAT IS ALREADY CREDENTIAL-AGNOSTIC, which shows the fix is small:
lines 515 and 560 speak of "whose credential identity is `userUri`",
which holds for any credential type that carries an identity. Only the
two places above hard-code Basic.

PROPOSED, for Mark:
- §keypackage: reject a credential whose TYPE the server does not
  support, rather than any credential that is not Basic. Say that a
  server MUST support Basic and MAY support others, and that whichever
  it supports, the credential's identity MUST be `userUri`.
- §senders: take the user URI from the leaf credential's identity for
  any supported credential type, not from Basic specifically.
- Optionally advertise the supported credential types in the
  account-level capability object beside `cipherSuites`, which already
  exists there, so a client knows before it tries.

WHY NOW: bead mimid-1wgh.99 is about to implement from this family, and
mimid-7yn7.4 records that identity past BasicCredential stops being a
documented weakness and becomes an exploitable asymmetry if interop is
mandated. A binding that forbids the stronger credential is the
narrowest place that gets fixed.

Not posted. Editing the draft is a write to ~/PROJECT/jmap-chat-spec and
needs Mark's approval per write.
notes: FIXED 2026-11-23 in jmap-chat-spec commit 377bddb, Mark approved. His principle, which is better than what this bead proposed: 'hard requiring basic was a mistake, it should each just be that the connection should be authorized and not dictate how.' That made the fix smaller than planned, because §keypackage ALREADY required the credential identity to be userUri -- the authorization was present and the Basic clause was pure surplus, so it was simply deleted. §senders now reads the identity of the leaf credential whatever its type. Added a paragraph saying the document does not constrain the type, that identity == userUri is what authorizes, and that a server MAY reject a type it cannot verify; plus an optional credentialTypes field in the account capability so a client can learn the accepted types rather than discovering them from a rejected KeyPackage/set. Both X.509 (RFC 9420 §5.3) and did:webvh are now usable through the binding. Renders clean through kramdown-rfc2629 and xml2rfc with no unresolved references.
